findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed the mop was stored with the mop head hanging from the outside edge of the mop bucket where it will drip onto the floor. PIC moved mop and emptied the mop bucket during the inspection. Ensure that mops are always stored in a position that allows the head to air-dry.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Other employee’s Food Handler certificate has expired, and will be renewed by the next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the sanitizer bucket was testing at 0 ppm (Cl) when the inspector arrived. The PIC was informed and they immediately remade the bucket. After being remade the bucket was too strong but after adding more water it tested at 150 ppm (Cl). The inspector educated that buckets must be checked on a regular basis using test strips and they cannot have any dish soap inside. Ensure that sanitizer buckets are always testing at the correct concentration.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed two coolers at the front area were not cold holding foods at 41F or below:

(1) The Coca-Cola cooler was holding cooked meat at an internal temperature of 45F. The PIC stated the meat was cooked earlier today. The only another items in the cooler are soda drinks. The meat was moved into a different cooler that was holding foods at 41F or below. Coca-Cola coolers are designed for drink storage not for cold holding TCS (temperature control for safety) foods. The inspector suggests not holding any TCS foods in the Coca-Cola cooler.

(2) The small white mini fridge was holding open jars of jalapeños and pickles (both stated they must be refrigerated after opening) and cream cheese. The temperature of a probe set in between two packages of cream cheese was 46F. The PIC turned up the temperature of the mini fridge during the inspection. The temperature of the cooler was observed to be going down at the end of the inspection. 

Ensure the temperature of all cold holding units at the facility are closely monitored to ensure foods are being maintained at 41F or less.

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Tile in the kitchen is in need of replacement. Several tile are broken throughout the facility. These areas are not smooth and easily cleanable. Replace damaged tile in the kitchen. 

Physical facilities in the kitchen have residue and debris accumulating from use. Ensure that the floors, corners, walls, and shutters are cleaned. 

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.comment: Observed food equipment to be placed in soiled "clean" area. Ensure equipment is placed in clean area. Clean areas as needed to prevent soil accumulation. Corrected. PIC will clean containers. Reference 4-601.11(A).

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.comment:
Observed beef being thawed in stagnant water. All TCS foods must be properly thawed in accordance to one of the four stated methods. Thaw TCS foods appropriately.
750-240 Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the  following method. 1. Under refrigeration 41°F or below, 2. Under  potable running water 70°F or below or below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, 4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 - Employee was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without use of a barrier. Proper handwashing was discussed. Proper handwashing technique poster was provided.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles. Use paper towels to dry hands, and then use paper towels as a barrier to shut off the faucet to avoid contaminating freshly washed hands.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Sani-bucket was not registering a bleach concentration and was just prepared. More bleach was added to the solution to obtain a concentration of 100ppm. Use test strips to verify solutions are at proper concentration (concentration based on label instructions).

Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.citation_text:
750.540 - Operator's FSSMC expired on 9/23/17 but is scheduled to take a food manager course on March 7 at Saint John's. Business card was provided for operator to contact inspector once certification is received. Provide certification number and expiration date prior to scheduled re-inspection date of 5/23/18 to avoid a re-inspection fee.

Class I facilities must employ an adequate number of certified food managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.
NOTE: Also maintain copies of food manger certifications for all staff at the facility.

findings.title: Facilities to maintain proper temperatures
findings.comment: Observed the reach in cooler next to the upright freezer to have an internal air temperature of 54 F. Food in the cooler was recorded between 28 F and 39 F. All food was moved to a properly functioning cooler to correct the violation.  Do not store potentially hazardous food in this unit until it can maintain proper cold holding temperature (41 F or below).  Repair or replace the unit.  Inspector will SPOT CHECK the unit on or shortly after 9/15/16. 750-140 All refrigeration units used to store potentially hazardous foods shall be able to maintain proper product temperature at 41°F or below.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.comment: Observed no thermometer in the pesi display cooler. During inspection, facility is storing potato salad and cole slaw in the bottom of the unit. Management provided a thermometer to correct the violation. 750.140(a) All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

findings.title: Lighting provided as required.  Fixtures shielded
